docker.note: build is FALSE and build_images is EMPTY, unlike V1 -- the image arrives via the docker_image member, so there is nothing to build. ensure_compose_images() still guards the outcome: it inspects the tag after restore and would fall back to building from the shipped Dockerfile if the load had somehow not produced it. tortoise-radio is intentionally NOT in containers[]; only its read-only bind mounts are archived.

prefix.note: The 'Turtle WoW' client shortcut runs under Proton Experimental and Steam manages the prefix itself, so nothing is archived -- but the compatibility tool must be set on the shortcut after restore, since the appid carries no CompatToolMapping entry.

edits.note: must read exactly `set realmlist 127.0.0.1` with NO leading space -- a leading space causes an instant disconnect at login. Same file V1 uses; both servers listen on 3724, so one realmlist serves either.

steam._note: informational only; the account is detected per-machine at restore
steam.grid_note: neither shortcut has grid artwork on this machine, so extras ships none

systemd_system_units.name: tortoise-radio-hosts.service
systemd_system_units.note: re-applies the /etc/hosts pins after a SteamOS update wipes them

runtime_deps.note: 1.5 G, not archived - Steam installs it. Set it on the 'Turtle WoW' shortcut via Properties > Compatibility.

reclaim.note: The client and the radio stack are ARCHIVED by this pack but deliberately NOT in reclaim paths, and are pinned in never_touch instead. Both are shared with Turtle WoW V1, whose pack also claims them; reclaiming V2 must never delete the client out from under V1. When V1 is finally retired, remove ~/Games/TurtleWoW and ~/tortoise-radio by hand rather than widening this list.

accounts.note: GM account, rank 3 -- the fleet-standard main account

members.note: Unlike V1, NO compiled binaries live here -- V2's Dockerfile compiles inside the image and CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/turtle is baked in, so the server lives in the docker_image member below. What ships here is data/ (3.1 G of dbc/maps/vmaps/mmaps, the expensive part), etc/ (the tuned configs incl. 1000 playerbots), src/ (needed because ./src/sql is bind-mounted at runtime by the DB auto-updater), and the compose file. data/mmaps is root-owned but 0755/0644, so plain tar reads it fine and it restores as deck -- no root_tar_zst needed, unlike Talisman's 0750 datadir. logs/ is root-owned debris and excluded.

THE SERVER ITSELF. V2's Dockerfile is a real two-stage compile (Debian trixie, GCC 14, BUILD_PLAYERBOTS=ON) whose output exists nowhere on the host -- only inside this image at /opt/turtle. Rebuilding it on a fresh Deck is a multi-hour job, so the built image ships. Restore does `docker load`, and ensure_compose_images() then finds the tag already present and skips the build. If this member is ever dropped, the Dockerfile is still shipped and restore will fall back to compiling -- correct, but slow.

MariaDB 10.6 data dir (~700 M): the 4 databases, the 500 bot accounts + 4500 bot characters, and the mmodad/player accounts. Archived at rest -- pack refuses while tw2-db runs. 10.6 and NOT 11.8 on purpose: create_databases.sql is a 10.6 dump using utf8mb4_general_ci. The image tag is pinned in docker-compose.yml so the on-disk format matches on restore.

The .radio stack, shipped in full because V2 is becoming the main build and V1 will eventually be deleted -- this pack must not depend on tortoise-wow-1.0.dmlpack still existing. nginx/icecast config, fix-hosts.sh, the systemd unit, ./music + ./wow-music. Bind-mounted read-only, so it is safe to tar while the container runs, which is why tortoise-radio is NOT in containers[]. Its radio-cache VOLUME is deliberately not archived: it is a proxy cache of the OctoWow relay and refills on demand.

The SAME 11 G client V1 uses -- build 7272, and V2 was built to match it exactly. Duplicated with tortoise-wow-1.0.dmlpack on purpose: V2 is the main build now and must restore standalone. Data/ is 9.4 G of already-compressed MPQs, so this member drops to zstd -3; -12 would burn CPU for almost nothing. WDB is excluded deliberately: a stale itemcache.wdb masks server-side item_template edits and has caused confusing bugs before. NOTE: if the Turtle client is ever updated, the stock mapextractor CRASHES on it (glibc _int_malloc assertion in old libmpq), so re-extracting data/ would become a real blocker -- see the handoff.

files.note: shared by 25+ launchers; never overwrite a newer one
